explorations.title: Certainty versus equal outcomes
explorations.instruction: Predict: with four outcomes, will making one weight large and the rest zero lower or raise entropy_bits compared with four equal weights? Then apply the preset, which sets n and log_weights.
explorations.observe: probabilities becomes [1,0,0,0] and contributions becomes [0,0,0,0], so entropy_bits reads 0 and normalized_entropy reads 0. Resetting the weights to [1,1,1,1,1,1] gives probabilities [0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25], each contribution 0.5 bits, and entropy_bits equal to 2.
explorations.why: When one probability is 1, its surprise log2(1/1) is 0 and the other outcomes carry probability 0, so every contribution is 0 and the choice is fully resolved; with four equal probabilities each carries 0.25 times 2 bits, which sums to the log2 4 = 2 bit maximum.

explorations.title: Adding a seventh half of the mass
explorations.instruction: Predict: if outcome 4's weight becomes 3 while outcomes 1 to 3 keep weight 1 and n is 3, what happens to total and to each probability? Then apply the preset, which sets n, log_weights and include_fourth.
explorations.observe: total rises from 3 to 6, probabilities changes from [0.333,0.333,0.333,0,0,0] to [0.167,0.167,0.167,0.5,0,0], the self-information of outcome 4 appears as 1 bit, its contribution is 0.5 bits, and entropy_bits falls from about 1.585 bits to about 1.792 bits after the extra term is added.
explorations.why: The include_fourth toggle lets w_4 enter the partition even when n is 3, so it dilutes the other three probabilities by half while adding its own p log2(1/p) term of 0.5 bits; the extra spread of the distribution raises the total, showing that entropy counts all outcomes with nonzero weight rather than only the first n.
